document.title: Cable from Amembassy Islamabad for Under Secretary Armacost and Ambassador Dean from Raphel. "Subject: Indo-Pakistani Relations"
document.authors: Ambassador Arnold Raphel, U.S. Embassy Islamabad
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Raphel agrees with Dean that Pakistan looks beyond the Soviet withdrawal to a new great game and a grand Islamic coalition from Turkey to Pakistan. For Americans the withdrawal is the victory; for South Asians it is only the first act.

events.description: Raphel cables Washington and Delhi assessing Indo-Pakistani views on Afghanistan after Soviet withdrawal.
Zia dissolves the Assembly and dismisses Prime Minister Junejo.
Raphel sends EXDIS cable on Indo-Pakistani relations and Afghanistan's future to Armacost and Dean.
Zia dissolved the assembly and dismissed Junejo.
Raphel and Charlie Wilson told Zia that relations would face hazards unless he moved to free and fair elections; Zia said he understood.

key_claims: Pakistan sees the chance for a friendly Afghanistan for the first time in 40 years, giving strategic depth against India.
Pakistanis are pleased by the prospect of an Islamic bloc stretching from Turkey to Pakistan, while Indians are worried.
Raphel argues Zia's dissolution of the Assembly was not driven by Afghan strategy, since a pro-Pakistani Islamic Afghanistan had universal support in Pakistan.
Junejo's unwillingness to push Zia's Islamization program was a reason for his dismissal.
Raphel believes Zia knows the U.S. will not shield him from anti-democratic actions.
